title: Zero-temperature SK full support, explained
h1: No missing overlap scales: the zero-temperature SK order parameter has full support
lead: Take any order parameter γ that minimizes the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure, zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model. Then its Stieltjes measure charges every neighbourhood of every point of [0,1): γ strictly increases, with no flat stretch anywhere below 1. Along the optimally steered random path X, the expected squared gradient of the value function equals t and the expected squared curvature equals 1. The Lean theorem full_support states this; it assumes a minimizer is given and does not prove that one exists.
desc: Unofficial plain-English explainer of the Lean theorem OAI.ZeroTemperatureSK.full_support in openai/math: every minimizer of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure SK model has full support on [0,1).
startNote: The statement and its 16 definitions are identical, character for character, in two upstream files: the Comparator challenge ComparatorChallenges/SKFullSupport.lean (where the theorem ends in a deliberate sorry: it is the target) and the proof's own Model.lean (lines 12–88), which this site links to. The proof itself is in Main.lean. Paper references are to the September 27, 2026 manuscript Full support of the zero-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick order parameter (OpenAI).
sizeNote: About 20,000 lines of Lean in 135 files (lean/OAI/Probability/SKSupport), importing only Mathlib.
agentCtx: the Lean proof that every minimizer of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure zero-field SK model has full support on [0,1) (openai/math, lean/OAI/Probability/SKSupport)

gloss.ContinuousOn: continuous at every point of the given set, using only points of that set
gloss.ContinuousWithinAt: continuous at a point when approached from within a set; with Set.Ici t this is right-continuity at t
gloss.ENNReal.ofReal: a real number as an extended nonnegative real (negative numbers become 0)
gloss.Filtration.natural: the filtration generated by a process: at each time, the events determined by the process up to that time
gloss.Integrable: the function's absolute value has finite integral (Lebesgue/Bochner)
gloss.IsBrownianReal: the process is a standard one-dimensional Brownian motion under the given measure
gloss.IsProgressive: progressively measurable for a filtration: on each time window [0,s], the process is jointly measurable in time and sample using only information available at s
gloss.Measurable: measurable as a function between measurable spaces
gloss.Monotone: nondecreasing: x ≤ y implies f x ≤ f y
gloss.Real.toNNReal: a real number as a nonnegative real, with negative numbers sent to 0 (used to index B and X by real times)
gloss.Set.Iic: the ray (−∞, b] (inside Time, the points ≤ b, i.e. [0, b])
gloss.Set.range: the set of all values a function takes
gloss.deriv: the derivative of a one-variable function at a point, defined to be 0 where the function is not differentiable
gloss.sSup: the least upper bound of a set of reals (Lean's convention: 0 for a set that is empty or unbounded above)
